unmapped_findings: Carbon partitioning coefficient of carbon in κ-carbide = 2.1 for the 0.59% Si steel aged 60 h at 530 °C (versus 2.9 for the 1.56% Si steel); silicon partitions to austenite during aging and decreases the austenite lattice parameter, increasing the κ–γ constrained mismatch (b0021).

Age-hardened 0.59% Si (0.002% P) specimens showed the lowest dynamic fracture toughness among the low-phosphorus silicon-containing steels in Table IV, which the authors attribute to a larger amount of porosity (b0079).

Porosity (micro-defects) in the 0.59% Si steel was more than twice that of the 1.07% Si steel and almost double that of the 1.56% Si steel; total inclusion density was similar among the three low-P silicon steels at 62–78 inclusions/mm² (b0079, Figure 15).

Parent solution-treated condition (1050 °C 2 h) of the same 0.59% Si, 0.002% P alloy: hardness 200 ± 10 BHN and dynamic fracture toughness 715 kJ/m² (Table IV, b0075). This belongs to the solution-treated (parent) process, not the aged condition.
Solution-treated 0.59% Si steel shows no spinodal decomposition or short-range ordering within the austenite, regardless of Si content, as confirmed by XRD and TEM (b0021).
